subject: DPA addendum: no-train + subprocessor routing — Helix Health
messages:
From: Nate Choi <nate@helixhealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@helixhealth.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Apr 2025 09:24:00 -0700
Subject: Data use addendum: no-train ask + subprocessors

Hi Marcus / Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — our product team loved the latency profile. Legal is now reviewing a DPA addendum tied to model-improvement/no-train commitments and a tighter subprocessor list. Key asks:

- A clear contractual "no-training" (no model improvement) commitment for tenant data used via the hosted API.
- Visibility on the subprocessor roster and a process for notifying changes (30 days).
- Onshore KMS or on-prem keywrap requirement for PHI in white-glove pilots.
- Exportability of prompt/response logs for audit (SFTP or API) with retention controls.

Can you confirm which of these we can commit to in an addendum and what pieces will require an implementation timeline? I attached a short matrix of our procurement priorities.

Attachments: procurement_terms_matrix.xlsx (xlsx)

—Nate
Nate Choi
Sr. Procurement Manager, Helix Health
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Nate Choi <nate@helixhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Apr 2025 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Data use addendum: no-train ask + subprocessors

Nate — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front:

- No-training commitment: yes, we can provide a contractual no-training clause for tenant interactions on the hosted API and Dedicated tiers. We will include language that we will not use customer-provided prompts/responses to update model weights or training datasets.

- Subprocessor roster & change notice: yes. We can provide current roster and a 30-day notice commitment for additions, with an option for onshore-only routing for a subset of customers (requires routing policy config).

- Onshore KMS / keywrap: we support customer-managed keys (KMS) in our Dedicated offering and can discuss an on-prem keywrap for pilot. For hosted customers, we offer KMS integrations in certain regions — we should align on which environment this pilot targets.

- Exportability: we provide API and SFTP options for audit exports; retention is configurable per-customer. Note: for exports containing PHI we recommend SFTP + HSM-backed key wrap.

I'll attach a first-pass DPA addendum and we can iterate. Can you loop in Alexa from legal so we can walk through the redlines?

Attachments: Helix_DPA_Addendum_v1.pdf (pdf)

Best,
Marcus
Marcus Lin
Director, Commercial — Redwood Inference

Marcus / Marissa — thanks for the quick reply. Two follow-ups from legal:

1) Wording: We need the no-training clause to cover both direct model training and sharing data with third-party model trainers (i.e., no transfer to any vendor that could use the data to improve models). Is Redwood willing to commit that subprocessor contracts will include the same prohibition?

2) Evidence & audit: For procurement, we need an ops checklist or runbook describing how you prevent tenant data from being used for model improvement (e.g., isolation of logs, KV cache policies, internal dev access controls). A short exhibit is fine.

I've attached a redline with small edits and comments.
